answer: Registering an identity is not a flat fee: within any funding cluster the bond rises with position, so the first account locks one unit, the second two, the third three, and the k-th locks k units, a river that gets steeper with every drop. Bonds thaw in a glacier for thirty epochs, so that capital is unavailable for the whole attack, and a cluster counts as one seat until its bonds thaw. Each account carries a pigment mark derived from its cluster, so a farm thousandth identity costs a thousand times the base bond. Honest newcomers pay one unit, since they open no cluster of their own.
